$comment: The house brand. This is what the product wears when it is selling itself:
the marketing site, the platform-admin console, the demo tenant, and the
'powered by' line in every customer's footer.
Sourced from the ifBash Brand Kit, September 2026 (tokens rev 2026-09-24):
brand/ifbash-brand-guide.md and brand/tokens/ifbash-tokens.json. Section
references below point at the guide. It replaces the Brick & Charcoal
edition of 2026-07-27. Questions go to brand@ifbash.com, not into this file.
Guide section 3. Aubergine is the brand; rose is coloured text and links;
mint is the accent because it is the one practice colour that passes as
text on paper and is meant to be seen at 5%. Peach is deliberately absent:
it is 'the agent', fills only, one object per screen — a token the UI
repeats in every card grid cannot honour that.
$overrides_note: Values the guide pins exactly, so they are not left to derivation.
Ink 50 (#8A6F7C) is non-text only, so every text tier is ink or ink 70.
Primary buttons are an ink fill with a paper label (section 6).
color.$darkOverrides_note: Guide section 6, 'Dark UI': raised panels, a plum rule, paper text, silver secondary, the on-dark practice stops, a paper button with an ink label, and a peach focus ring (rose fails on the field at 2.42:1).

$comment: Guide section 4 and brand/fonts/FONTS.md. Three families, strictly divided.
Bricolage ships Bold only and is declared across 700-800, as the kit does.
Hanken SemiBold is declared across 600-700 so a bold request gets the real
600 drawing rather than a faux-bolded one; the guide emphasises with 600.
No italic is shipped, by design.

shape.$comment: Guide section 5: radius 2px, no shadows, structure from hairlines. 'none' is the nearest named radius.

$comment: Guide section 2. Never recolour or redraw these. The favicon is the
transparent mark that flips aubergine/paper with the browser theme, not
the app tile (section 2b). No ogImage: the kit's cards are post templates,
so the portal renders its own card from these colours.

copy.tagline: The alumni network your college actually owns.
copy.heroHeadline: Your alumni are not a mailing list.
copy.heroSubhead: A verified directory, a working referral channel between final-years and graduates, and a records layer that survives the person who set it up. Built for Indian engineering colleges, on infrastructure that stays in India.
